chunks.title: Fan Model and Overview
chunks.content: Haiku ceiling fan model L3127 uses DC motor with permanent magnetics and hand-balanced Thin Sheet airfoils for efficient, quiet airflow.

chunks.title: Optional Wall Control Accessory
chunks.content: A Haiku Wall Control accessory can be added for SenseME smart technology and can connect fans to a Nest Learning Thermostat to save up to 30% on HVAC costs.

chunks.title: Use Comfort Modes
chunks.content: Sleep Mode gradually reduces fan speed hourly until the lowest set speed, then turns off; Timer Mode runs the fan at a set speed until time expires; Whoosh Mode silently varies fan speed to simulate a natural breeze.

chunks.title: Operate the Remote Control
chunks.content: Use Power to turn the fan on/off, Speed arrows to adjust fan speed, Light button and arrows to control on/off and brightness, Timer button (press 1-7 times) to set auto-off, Whoosh to activate breeze mode after setting max speed, and Sleep (with Timer) to activate Sleep Mode.

chunks.title: Remote Control Battery
chunks.content: The remote operates on a single CR2025 3V lithium coin cell battery.

chunks.title: Reverse Fan Direction
chunks.content: To reverse the fan, press Power to turn it off, wait for a complete stop, then press Whoosh three times followed by Power; repeat to return to forward operation. Haiku recommends simply running the fan at a slow speed in winter instead of reversing it.

chunks.title: Fan Won't Start / Power Issues
chunks.content: Check that supply power is adequate, circuit breaker/fuse and wall switch function, and that all wiring is secure and properly grounded.

rows: Verify that supply power is adequate. Check your circuit breaker or fuse and wall switch for functionality.
Make sure that all wires are securely connected and the fan is properly wired and grounded.

chunks.title: Fan Noisy During Operation
chunks.content: Check all mounting and fan hardware for looseness and tighten; ensure no fan parts rub against the motor unit while rotating.

rows: The fan is noisy during operation
Check all mounting and fan hardware. If loose, tighten.
The fan is noisy during operation
Make sure there are no fan parts rubbing on the motor unit when the fan rotates.

chunks.title: Startup Jerk, LED Flashing, Fan Wobble
chunks.content: Slight jerking on startup is normal; LED flashing indicates a mode/speed change notification; wobble is fixed by securing mounting hardware and ensuring airfoils are aligned and fastened (replace airfoils only as a full set, never individually).

rows: This is normal and may happen occasionally upon startup. An initial slight jerking forward and backward does not affect fan operation.
Why are the LED indicators flashing?
The LED indicators flash when an operating mode is being adjusted to notify you when the fan has changed speeds or modes.

Make sure that all mounting hardware is secure and tight. Make sure that all the airfoils are aligned properly and are securely fastened to the fan hub. Airfoils must be replaced as a set. Do not replace individual airfoils. If an airfoil is damaged, contact Haiku Customer Service.

chunks.title: Do Not Replace Individual Airfoils
chunks.content: If an airfoil is damaged, it must be replaced along with the full set rather than individually, and Haiku Customer Service should be contacted for replacement parts.

chunks.title: Annual Maintenance Checklist
chunks.content: Once a year, check the safety cable, secure mounting and airfoil hardware, verify wiring/ground connections, and clean the airfoils to ensure safe, efficient operation.

chunks.title: Clean Airfoils Properly
chunks.content: Dust airfoils regularly and clean with a damp cloth using ordinary soap and water only; never use solvents, gasoline, or other chemical cleaners as they can distort and damage the fan surface.

tasks.title: Check Safety Cable
tasks.description: Verify the fan's safety cable and hardware are properly installed each year.
tasks.justification: A failed or missing safety cable could allow the fan to fall if the mounting fails, posing a physical hazard.
tasks.instructions_text: Slide the wiring cover down the extension tube and visually examine the safety cable and its attaching hardware for proper installation and wear.

tasks.title: Secure Mounting and Airfoil Hardware
tasks.description: Check and tighten the mounting hardware and the hardware holding the airfoils to the fan hub once a year.
tasks.justification: Loose hardware can cause wobble, noise, and eventual fan damage or an airfoil coming loose.
tasks.instructions_text: Inspect all mounting bolts and airfoil fasteners and tighten any that are loose using the appropriate tool.

tasks.title: Check Wiring and Ground Connection
tasks.description: Inspect the wire nuts and ground wire connection once a year to ensure they remain secure.
tasks.justification: Loose wiring or a disconnected ground wire creates an electrical shock or fire hazard.
tasks.instructions_text: Open the wiring cover and check that all wire nuts are tight and the ground wire is securely fastened.

tasks.title: Clean the Airfoils
tasks.description: Dust the fan airfoils regularly, and wipe them with a damp cloth using mild soap and water if they get dirty.
tasks.justification: Cosmetic dust buildup is removed; using harsh chemicals instead could distort or damage the airfoil surface.
tasks.instructions_text: Dust the airfoils with a soft cloth regularly. If dirty, wipe with a damp cloth using ordinary soap and water.

tasks.title: Replace Remote Control Battery
tasks.description: Replace the CR2025 lithium battery in the remote control when it stops responding.
tasks.justification: A depleted battery prevents the remote from controlling the fan and light.
tasks.instructions_text: Open the battery compartment on the back of the remote, remove the old CR2025 battery, insert a new one, and properly dispose of the old battery.

deep_clean.title: Annual Fan Cleaning and Inspection
steps: Check the safety cable by sliding the wiring cover down the extension tube and examining the cable and hardware.
Verify mounting hardware and airfoil-to-hub hardware are securely fastened.
Check that wire nuts are secure and the ground wire is properly connected.
